pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Business quality is average: scale is real, but earnings are cyclical and only partly contracted. Precision averaged 73 active Canadian rigs and 43 U.S. rigs in the third quarter, 35.96% of the Canadian industry count, but term contracts covered only 43.90% of active rigs and 59.33% of nine-month revenue came from Canada, where seasonality limits utilization. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B12

Margins are the weakest dimension. EBITDA margin was 23.53% in the third quarter against 25.45% a year earlier and 27.70% in the first quarter of 2025, because U.S. operating cost per utilization day rose 14.67% on rig reactivations while Canadian cost per day was flat to lower. Basis: calculation B1; calculation B9; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-10-27_exh_991.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4

Cash conversion is thin and falling. Free cash flow was 16.09% of nine-month EBITDA against 28.83% a year earlier, capital expenditures rose to 14.82% of revenue from 13.34%, and cash from operations less capital expenditures was negative CAD 12 million in the third quarter, so little cash is left for debt reduction after buybacks. Basis: calculation B3; calculation B4; calculation B13; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Leverage and liquidity are the main support. Total debt was 1.33x and net debt 1.28x last-twelve-months EBITDA, liquidity was CAD 462 million, and the company reports senior debt at 0.14x covenant EBITDA against a limit of 2.50x and covenant interest cover of 10.27x against a floor of 2.50x, so near-term covenant and liquidity stress is remote on the reported figures. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-10-27_exh_991.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13; calculation B13

Financial policy is mixed rather than creditor-aligned. Buybacks were between 62.27% and 83.65% of free cash flow on three definitions against a guideline of up to 50%, while net debt rose and the stated target of net debt below 1.0x EBITDA is not met; the debt reduction target of CAD 100 million has CAD 75 million done. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation B12

Refinancing risk sits in 2028 and 2029. The Senior Credit Facility matures in October 2028 and the notes in January 2029 are 89.69% of principal, and the notes' disclosed fair value of about CAD 569 million is close to their principal, a neutral signal, but no ratings, prices or peers are supplied to test market access. Basis: calculation B5; Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-10-27_exh_992.htm.jsonl, page 11

The tax dispute is the largest contingent claim. The company states a maximum liability of CAD 155 million excluding interest and must pay half, up to CAD 77.5 million, once reassessments are issued, which is 3.34x its cash and 16.76% of liquidity. Basis: calculation B6; 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-10-27_exh_992.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13

Near-term outlook is constructive and medium-term outlook is not established. Management guides fourth-quarter operating margin per utilization day to CAD 13,500 to CAD 14,500 in Canada and US$9,500 to US$10,500 in the U.S., up 5.33% to 13.13% and 24.13% to 37.20% on the third quarter, but gives no multi-year projections. Basis: calculation B7; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-10-27_exh_991.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 7

runs.text: The first strength is moderate leverage with ample liquidity. Net debt of CAD 606 million is 1.28x LTM EBITDA, liquidity of CAD 462 million sits against a maturity wall that starts in October 2028, and secured debt is small at 0.14x covenant EBITDA, so near-term refinancing and covenant risk is low. Basis: calculation B12; Financial foundation (CP-1)

The second strength is market position with a growing contract book. Precision holds 35.96% of Canadian industry rigs and a rising share in the U.S., and average term rigs rose to 54 in the third quarter from 43 in the first, which adds revenue visibility and supports customer-funded upgrades. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B12

The third strength is disclosure. The company prints quarterly statements, a facility-by-facility liquidity table and covenant results, which lets creditors monitor leverage and headroom as events develop. Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-10-27_exh_991.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The first weakness is margin pressure. EBITDA margin fell from 27.70% in the first quarter of 2025 to 23.53% in the third quarter of 2026 as U.S. reactivation costs and international mix offset higher volumes, which cuts the cash available to repay debt. Basis: calculation B1; calculation B9

The second weakness is thin free cash flow against policy. Free cash flow conversion fell to 16.09% of EBITDA while buybacks took most of it, so net debt rose and cash is CAD 23 million, which leaves the debt reduction target dependent on a strong fourth quarter. Basis: calculation B3; calculation B12

The third weakness is the 2028 and 2029 refinancing concentration, with the notes 89.69% of principal, combined with an unresolved tax dispute of up to CAD 155 million excluding interest, half of it payable on reassessment. Basis: calculation B5; calculation B6

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: No acquisition, sponsor transaction, leveraged buyout, recapitalisation or new debt issue is stated in the sources for 2026. The financing changes are repayments: the company repaid CAD 75 million of Senior Credit Facility borrowings net of new draws over nine months, and it still has the secured facility and the unsecured senior notes due 2029 outstanding. Capital transactions are customer upgrades to 25 drilling rigs backed by long-term contracts, a pending upgrade opportunity for a large Canadian producer that would have multiple rigs contracted through 2029, and a second five-year Kuwait contract for an existing rig, none of which adds debt in the sources. Share repurchases of CAD 47 million were made under the normal course issuer bid with an automated share purchase plan. Basis: calculation A10; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-07-28_exh_991.htm.jsonl, page 2; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-10-27_exh_991.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 6, 8; 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-10-27_exh_992.htm.jsonl, page 10

fields.value: PRECISION DRILLING Corp (issuer id pds), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the financial foundation: normalised statements, debt, liquidity, leverage and interest cover at September 30, 2026 and the three earlier reporting dates, on the issuer's consolidated statements in Canadian dollars.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is moderate but has not improved on a net basis: net debt was 1.28x last-twelve-months EBITDA at September 30, 2026 against 1.21x at December 31, 2025, while total debt eased to 1.33x from 1.39x, so further deleveraging depends on cash generation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Refinancing risk is low for now because only a small secured facility is drawn and the large unsecured notes mature in January 2029, but cash of CAD 23 million is thin after share buybacks and capital spending, and a disclosed Canadian tax reassessment of up to CAD 155 million excluding interest is not provided for. Full-year 2025 statements were not supplied, so fiscal 2025 earnings are rebuilt from the four reported quarters and the year-end balance sheet comes from the 2026 comparatives.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Gross debt fell by CAD 50 million over nine months to CAD 629 million, but net debt rose by CAD 12 million to CAD 606 million because cash fell from CAD 86 million to CAD 23 million, by more than debt did, and LTM EBITDA slipped to CAD 473 million from CAD 490 million. The company repaid CAD 75 million of facility borrowings net of new draws, repurchased CAD 47 million of shares and saw cash fall by CAD 63 million, against free cash flow of CAD 56 million; a weaker Canadian dollar added CAD 23 million to the carrying value of the U.S. dollar debt. Creditors therefore see lower gross debt than at the start of the year without a better net position.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: EBITDA recovered to CAD 125 million in the third quarter from CAD 97 million in the second, but nine-month EBITDA of CAD 346 million is below the CAD 363 million of a year earlier, because of lower upfront capital payments in Canada, higher U.S. and international operating costs and higher share-based compensation. U.S. operating margin per utilization day fell to US$7,653 in the third quarter from US$8,700 a year earlier, and management guides to US$9,500 to US$10,500 for the fourth quarter, which is the main earnings assumption behind any deleveraging.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation is positive but thin after growth capital: nine-month cash from operations of CAD 280 million less capital expenditures of CAD 224 million leaves free cash flow of CAD 56 million, and the 2026 capital budget was raised to CAD 275 million to CAD 285 million, which implies CAD 51 million to CAD 61 million in the fourth quarter, with CAD 143 million of purchase commitments running to 2028. Cash interest paid was CAD 47 million for the nine months, which EBITDA less capital expenditures covers 2.63x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate: cash of CAD 23 million plus CAD 439 million of undrawn facilities gives CAD 462 million, consistent with the company's own statement of more than CAD 460 million. The secured Senior Credit Facility has US$46 million drawn against a US$375 million commitment that matures in October 2028, of which US$43 million expires in June 2027, and the company reports senior debt at 0.14x covenant EBITDA against a limit of 2.50x and covenant interest cover of 10.27x against a floor of 2.50x. The US$400 million unsecured senior notes mature in January 2029 and are the only large maturity, so the 2029 wall is the refinancing question.

Unadjusted EBITDA would be CAD 128 million for the third quarter against the printed CAD 125 million, a difference of 2.07%, so the measure used here is the more conservative of the two.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case against caution is the company's own reporting: senior debt is 0.14x covenant EBITDA, covenant interest cover is 10.27x and available liquidity exceeds CAD 460 million, with U.S. margins guided up for the fourth quarter and Canadian heavy oil activity strong, so net leverage could fall quickly if guidance is met. The view would improve if fourth-quarter U.S. operating margin per utilization day reaches the guided US$9,500 to US$10,500 and cash is rebuilt while buybacks continue. It would worsen if capital spending reaches the top of the revised budget without EBITDA growth, if reassessments for further tax years are issued, or if Middle East disruption cuts international margins further.

fields.value: Precision is a cyclical North American land driller with no sponsor or controlling shareholder disclosed, so creditors depend on rig margins and the company's own cash discipline, and that discipline is mixed: buybacks continued in 2026 while net debt rose.

fields.value: Revenue is concentrated in Canada at 59.33% of nine-month revenue and the United States at 32.09%, with 43.90% of third-quarter active rigs on term contracts, so earnings follow utilization and day-rate margins. International work is small and contracted into 2027 and 2028. Governance disclosure is thin because the annual information form, ownership and related-party detail were not supplied.

fields.value: Margin pressure is a U.S. execution issue rather than a pricing issue. U.S. revenue per utilization day rose to US$33,270 from US$31,040, but operating margin per day fell to US$7,653 from US$8,700 because six reactivated rigs carried reactivation costs of US$2,125 per day; management guides to US$9,500 to US$10,500 in the fourth quarter, which has not yet been reported.

fields.value: International is small, fixed-term and concentrated in two countries. Seven active rigs in Saudi Arabia and Kuwait sit on five-year contracts into 2027 and 2028 and produced 8.58% of nine-month revenue, but revenue per utilization day fell to US$46,304 from US$53,811 on rig mix and recertification days, and crew costs stay elevated while regional tension persists.

fields.value: The policy is shareholder-return led with a stated leverage cap, and ownership is public. No sponsor or controlling shareholder is disclosed; the company allocates up to 50% of free cash flow before debt repayments to buybacks, targets CAD 100 million of debt reduction in 2026 and a net debt to EBITDA ratio below 1.0x, and repaid CAD 75 million net of new borrowings in nine months.

The annual report describes a five-member audit committee of independent financial experts, yet one of those directors is listed in the annual report and the first quarter report but not in the second and third quarter reports with no stated reason, and the auditor is named differently in the annual report and in the interim reports.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against caution is operating strength and explicit policy limits. Precision held about 35.96% of Canadian industry rigs against 35.80% a year earlier, and its U.S. share rose to 7.48% from 6.86%, with customer upgrades to 25 rigs backed by long-term contracts and a pending upgrade opportunity that would put multiple rigs under contract through 2029 for a large Canadian producer; the contract book is also growing, with average term rigs of 54 in the third quarter against 43 in the first quarter, and the buyback guideline is capped as a share of free cash flow and tied to a debt reduction target. The view would improve if fourth-quarter U.S. operating margin per day reaches the guided range, buybacks slow to the stated pace and the board changes are explained. It would worsen if repurchases are funded by borrowing, if the credit facility is amended or waived, if further reassessments are issued, or if the audit committee loses members without disclosure.

fields.value: PRECISION DRILLING Corp (issuer id pds), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the fundamental credit synthesis: business quality, cash flow, leverage, liquidity, financial policy and the main downside path, built on Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Precision has an adequate but cyclical credit profile, with moderate leverage and no maturity before October 2028, so creditors face a margin and cash-flow squeeze rather than a liquidity event unless buybacks and capital spending outrun operating cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt was CAD 606 million, or 1.28x last-twelve-months EBITDA, with liquidity of CAD 462 million, but free cash flow was only CAD 56 million in nine months, EBITDA margins are below last year and the CAD 569 million notes mature in 2029. The primary downside path is a weak winter drilling season while buybacks continue, which at the weakest recent quarter's run-rate would lift net leverage to 1.56x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation B2; calculation B1; calculation B13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business quality is average: scale is real, but earnings are cyclical and only partly contracted. Precision averaged 73 active Canadian rigs and 43 U.S. rigs in the third quarter, 35.96% of the Canadian industry count, but term contracts covered only 43.90% of active rigs and 59.33% of nine-month revenue came from Canada, where seasonality limits utilization.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins are the weakest dimension. EBITDA margin was 23.53% in the third quarter against 25.45% a year earlier and 27.70% in the first quarter of 2025, because U.S. operating cost per utilization day rose 14.67% on rig reactivations while Canadian cost per day was flat to lower.

fields.value: Basis: calculation B1; calculation B9; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-10-27_exh_991.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4

fields.value: Cash conversion is thin and falling. Free cash flow was 16.09% of nine-month EBITDA against 28.83% a year earlier, capital expenditures rose to 14.82% of revenue from 13.34%, and cash from operations less capital expenditures was negative CAD 12 million in the third quarter, so little cash is left for debt reduction after buybacks.

fields.value: Leverage and liquidity are the main support. Total debt was 1.33x and net debt 1.28x last-twelve-months EBITDA, liquidity was CAD 462 million, and the company reports senior debt at 0.14x covenant EBITDA against a limit of 2.50x and covenant interest cover of 10.27x against a floor of 2.50x, so near-term covenant and liquidity stress is remote on the reported figures.

fields.value: Financial policy is mixed rather than creditor-aligned. Buybacks were between 62.27% and 83.65% of free cash flow on three definitions against a guideline of up to 50%, while net debt rose and the stated target of net debt below 1.0x EBITDA is not met; the debt reduction target of CAD 100 million has CAD 75 million done.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Near-term outlook is constructive and medium-term outlook is not established. Management guides fourth-quarter operating margin per utilization day to CAD 13,500 to CAD 14,500 in Canada and US$9,500 to US$10,500 in the U.S., up 5.33% to 13.13% and 24.13% to 37.20% on the third quarter, but gives no multi-year projections.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case against the cautious view is that the company can fund its policy and still delever: liquidity of CAD 462 million, covenant ratios far from their limits, a contract book that grew to an average of 54 term rigs in the third quarter from 43 in the first, customer upgrades backed by long-term contracts, and fourth-quarter margin guidance that is 24.13% to 37.20% higher per U.S. day. Oil prices also rose, with WTI up 32.28% and WCS up 34.65% year on year. The view would improve if fourth-quarter U.S. margins reach guidance, cash is rebuilt while the debt reduction target is met and net leverage moves below 1.0x. It would worsen if margins stay at third-quarter levels, buybacks continue at the current pace, capital spending reaches CAD 285 million, or tax reassessments are issued.

fields.value: The first strength is moderate leverage with ample liquidity. Net debt of CAD 606 million is 1.28x LTM EBITDA, liquidity of CAD 462 million sits against a maturity wall that starts in October 2028, and secured debt is small at 0.14x covenant EBITDA, so near-term refinancing and covenant risk is low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second strength is market position with a growing contract book. Precision holds 35.96% of Canadian industry rigs and a rising share in the U.S., and average term rigs rose to 54 in the third quarter from 43 in the first, which adds revenue visibility and supports customer-funded upgrades.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third strength is disclosure. The company prints quarterly statements, a facility-by-facility liquidity table and covenant results, which lets creditors monitor leverage and headroom as events develop.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first weakness is margin pressure. EBITDA margin fell from 27.70% in the first quarter of 2025 to 23.53% in the third quarter of 2026 as U.S. reactivation costs and international mix offset higher volumes, which cuts the cash available to repay debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second weakness is thin free cash flow against policy. Free cash flow conversion fell to 16.09% of EBITDA while buybacks took most of it, so net debt rose and cash is CAD 23 million, which leaves the debt reduction target dependent on a strong fourth quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third weakness is the 2028 and 2029 refinancing concentration, with the notes 89.69% of principal, combined with an unresolved tax dispute of up to CAD 155 million excluding interest, half of it payable on reassessment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Precision is an Alberta-based land driller and well-service provider with 184 contract drilling rigs and 150 service rigs, earning 59.33% of nine-month revenue in Canada, 32.09% in the United States and 8.58% internationally, almost all from day-rate and hourly services. Revenue is cyclical and discretionary to oil and gas producers, customers are not named, and term contracts cover 43.90% of active rigs, so cash-flow visibility is partial and debt service capacity depends on utilization and day-rate margins. Variable operating costs and customer-funded upgrades preserve liquidity in a downturn, which supports refinancing confidence, but a mid-cycle slowdown would pass quickly to cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Precision is publicly listed in Toronto and New York with no sponsor or controlling shareholder disclosed, so no sponsor support or extraction is evidenced and financial policy is set by the board. Subsidiaries, obligors and guarantors are not named, so structurally senior claims are not established and the secured facility and unsecured notes cannot be ranked beyond the company's own labels. Policy is mixed: up to half of free cash flow before debt repayments goes to buybacks, the company targets CAD 100 million of 2026 debt reduction and net debt below 1.0x EBITDA, and an unexplained director list change and an auditor naming difference reduce confidence in governance facts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue follows rig utilization days and revenue per utilization day. Canadian days rose 15.8% and U.S. days 18.8% in the third quarter, U.S. revenue per day rose to US$33,270 from US$31,040 on day rates and technology revenue, Canadian revenue per day eased on rig mix and international revenue per day fell to US$46,304 from US$53,811. Third-quarter WTI was up 32.28% and WCS up 34.65%, which drives customer cash flow and demand. Revenue is therefore cyclical and activity-driven, not recurring, with limited pass-through evidence, which keeps pricing power average and leaves earnings exposed to a customer capital pullback.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The company states a variable operating cost structure with maintenance capital that responds to activity, but cost per day moved against it in 2026: U.S. cost per utilization day rose 14.67% as rigs were reactivated and international crew costs stay elevated, while share-based compensation moved EBITDA by CAD 19 million in the first quarter and a recovery in the second. Margins can be defended under volume growth with reactivation costs absorbed, but under volume pressure the fixed crew and reactivation costs would deleverage EBITDA faster than revenue, as the margin range of 21.43% to 27.70% across seven quarters shows.

fields.value: Basis: calculation B9; calculation B1; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-10-27_exh_991.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4, 7, 10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital expenditures were 14.82% of nine-month revenue, with CAD 139 million on maintenance and CAD 85 million on customer-driven upgrades, and the 2026 budget was raised to CAD 275 million to CAD 285 million with CAD 143 million of commitments to 2028, so capex flexibility is limited to the maintenance portion and the uncommitted growth portion. Free cash flow of 16.09% of EBITDA falls to 12.52% after lease payments, working capital absorbed cash seasonally, cash interest took 13.44% of EBITDA and cash taxes were small. EBITDA therefore converts only partly into free cash flow for deleveraging, and debt reduction depends on a seasonally stronger fourth quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry matters most: Precision's U.S. share is only 7.48% of industry rigs, so it is a price taker in a fragmented market, while its 35.96% Canadian share gives scale but not pricing control. Buyer power is high because producers focus on capital discipline and return, which keeps day rates tied to oil prices and limits margin recovery. New entrants are limited by capital intensity of rig upgrades, and substitutes and supplier power are not evidenced beyond delivery delays and long-lead items noted in the capital budget. These forces cap margin durability and so cap deleveraging speed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Political and economic factors are material to credit. The Middle East conflict raised international crew costs and oil prices, tariffs between Canada and the United States are noted as a source of volatility, and U.S. dollar debt is designated as a hedge of the net investment in U.S. operations, which limits the equity effect of exchange rates but not the Canadian dollar value of debt, which rose CAD 23 million in the year. Social and technological factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver on these materials.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths are moderate leverage, CAD 462 million of liquidity, a growing contract book and quarterly covenant disclosure. Weaknesses are margins down from earlier quarters, thin free cash flow after capital spending and buybacks, notes concentrated in 2029 and a tax dispute. Opportunities that could improve credit are the guided fourth-quarter margin recovery, customer-funded upgrades and contracted rigs through 2029. Threats that could weaken credit are an oil-price or customer capital pullback, international cost pressure, unexpected reassessments and higher interest costs at refinancing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B12; Business & governance (CP-1A); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-10-27_exh_991.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On a ratings-style lens, scale and market position are average, competitive advantage is average because technology claims are unproven, business diversification is average with three regions but one commodity, cost and capex flexibility is average, margin stability is weak, free cash flow stability is weak, ability to refinance is average with no market data, liquidity is strong in amount but thin in cash, and financial policy and governance is average with mixed alignment. The main supports are leverage of 1.33x and liquidity of CAD 462 million, the main constraints are margins and cash conversion, the trend is flat in net leverage and down in margin, and the missing datapoints are audited fiscal 2025 statements, legal terms and market prices.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B12; calculation B1; calculation B3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: For the next 12 to 24 months, management expects North American activity to stay resilient through the end of 2026 with growth potential emerging early in 2027, Canadian Super Series rigs nearly fully used in winter, and U.S. oil-directed activity strengthening, which supports utilization and the margin guidance for the fourth quarter. Egress capacity from LNG Canada and heavy oil demand are tailwinds; customer capital discipline, Middle East costs, margin lag and a CAD 143 million commitment profile are headwinds. A three to five year outlook is not established because the sources give no multi-year projections. Each tailwind supports revenue and margin recovery but does not by itself lower net debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The issuer-specific downside begins with a weak Canadian winter season or lower oil prices that make customers defer drilling, which first idles spot rigs and cuts utilization days in Canada and the U.S. while term rigs, 54 of 123 active in the third quarter, keep earning. Revenue and EBITDA fall faster than costs because crew and reactivation costs are sticky; at the weakest reported quarter's run-rate of CAD 388.22 million EBITDA, total debt would be 1.62x and net debt 1.56x, against 1.33x and 1.28x now. Free cash flow would turn negative if capex stays at budget, so management would need to cut buybacks and uncommitted upgrades; liquidity of CAD 462 million and covenant ratios far from limits suggest the company can avoid liquidity distress, but a cash call on half of the CAD 155 million tax claim would use CAD 77.5 million, and the 2029 notes would face refinancing at higher leverage.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B2; calculation B6; calculation B12; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-10-27_exh_991.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 8, 12–13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Precision presents an adequate but cyclical business profile supported by moderate leverage, liquidity and a growing contract book, but credit quality is constrained by margin pressure, thin free cash flow after buybacks and capital spending, and refinancing concentrated in 2028 and 2029. Cash-flow durability appears adequate in good conditions and weak in a downturn due to sticky costs and uneven conversion. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on fourth-quarter margins, the pace of net debt reduction and market conditions. The primary downside path is a weak drilling season with continued buybacks. Further analysis would require audited fiscal 2025 statements, the credit agreement and indenture, ratings and market prices. Fundamental credit analysis completed. Top risk: net leverage rising with thin cash.
